patterns.title: Random Definition — build and vary
patterns.description: Carry a familiar object into one new capacity. Give the student a reason, an explanation, a construction and a variation.
patterns.caution: Keep the exact inherited files available. A passing program does not prove that the student understands it.

sources.title: Ada writing patterns and prose samples

nodes.label: Notice a difference
nodes.information: One observable change in the carried object.
nodes.instruction: Describe a difference the student can see in the current hall.
nodes.gain: A reason to investigate this operation.
nodes.bridge: What would have to change in our existing object?

nodes.label: Recall the inheritance
nodes.information: The previous lesson, its object and usable code.
nodes.instruction: Name the exact inherited file and what the student already knows; link rather than reprint.
nodes.gain: A clear boundary between inherited and new work.
nodes.bridge: Which part of that inheritance cannot yet do this?

nodes.label: Define the new part
nodes.information: The new concept and the conditions it needs.
nodes.instruction: Define the operation, then name what it does to the carried data.
nodes.gain: A usable account of the mechanism.
nodes.bridge: What happens to a small concrete input?

nodes.label: Trace a case
nodes.information: A small input, intermediate state and result.
nodes.instruction: Follow the data step by step; let the student predict the last step.
nodes.gain: A mental model for reading the code.
nodes.bridge: Where will these steps appear in the program?

nodes.label: Build and run
nodes.information: Complete new code, setup and execution.
nodes.job: Turn the explanation into a working object.
nodes.instruction: Introduce the code event, supply complete new code, then point out the important lines.
nodes.gain: A reconstructable example with named dependencies.
nodes.bridge: Does its behaviour match the trace?

nodes.label: Predict and vary
nodes.information: One meaningful change and its expected consequence.
nodes.instruction: Ask for a prediction before changing one relation. Run behavioural assertions and explain the result.
nodes.gain: A capacity to modify the example deliberately.
nodes.bridge: What can the next hall take as already available?

nodes.label: Carry onward
nodes.information: The object, code and capacity retained.
nodes.instruction: Name what is kept and the next problem it makes possible.
nodes.gain: A reason for the next lesson.
nodes.bridge: The next hall puts the retained capacity to work.

trial.next: Adapt the trace, build and variation to local generator state, successive draws and RGB assignment; then judge the written passage.
